column2: Locks, shadowbans and limited-visibility warnings reported for engaging the wrong posts — and a witness who says the FBI told him to delete his own 4K footage. Whether or not any of it was coordinated, it decides which open-source evidence is still readable.

The routing table for the whole section: ballistics, GRAMA records, courtyard paving, aircraft, exploding-mic and Israel threads, each with its podcast lead and its X lead. Start here if you do not yet know which handle owns which question.

Proposed Law 4 would hand private citizens an FBI team, an intelligence team and full file access. Three hosts are the names most discussed for that role — this page sets out what each actually contributed.

This site's author, and a plain statement that almost nothing here originated here. It also carries the Battle Bun Brigade anthem, whose refrain — do not build a verdict with an empty hand — is the standard the rest of the site tries to hold.

The researcher who put N1098L at the centre of the case is also the man who killed the Egyptian-armada theory, citing decades-old Provo maintenance contracts. Someone who pushed the hardest aircraft claim and then refuted the second-hardest is the best evidence the plane work is not uniform conspiracy-building.

The distribution layer of the investigation — who said what, and where. Podcast hosts, X researchers and YouTube channels reaching hundreds of millions, indexed so a reader can find the GRAMA breakthrough or the ballistics deep-dive without hunting.

Twenty programs, from the largest podcast on earth to one-man research channels, mapped by what each one actually owns: ballistics guests, security interviews, foreign leads, motive. Mainstream television carried none of it.

InfoWars ran the case daily from September 10 onward and put ballistics specialists and Green Berets on live. Its host also read the ATF's "could not be identified or excluded" language as a non-match — the stronger reading is his inference, not a finding.

A former attorney worked sixteen search warrants into a minute-level timeline and found the pieces that will not fit: photos released after the suspect was already Mirandized, and a Discord message sent hours after that. His allegations, with the sealed records that would settle them named.

A decade-long TPUSA colleague said on camera there is "considerable evidence that there were state actors involved here" — and then stopped talking. He reportedly met the FBI director and the attorney general the next day, over death threats to his family.

Episode 287 is the most direct podcast treatment of the killing by any major host, from a woman who called Charlie her best friend and brother. She ran a tipline, published the SUV photographs, and became the primary target of the reported takedown campaigns.

The show ended mid-event. What is left is an archive of guests, appearances and statements from the final months — including the Tampa summit and the Virginia Tech stage six days before — and an open question about who controls it now.

He read private texts from Charlie on air, including the ones about Israel and donors. Two months before the killing he was given a TPUSA main stage to argue that case — a fact the donor-friction timeline treats as a data point in itself.

He describes a Hamptons gathering at which Kirk faced pro-Israel donor pressure. No attendee list or record of that meeting has been published, which is exactly why the claim sits here with its status marked rather than buried in a thread.

The most credentialed critic of the intelligence apparatus on this list, and the least easily dismissed as partisan. His lifelong subject — how agencies shape a narrative before the facts are in — is the exact shape of the foreign-leads dispute.

An amplification channel rather than a research one, and valuable for exactly that. Their Stew Peters episode carried the foreign-intelligence angle to an audience the analytical shows never reach, and their post is one source for the "break away from being pro-Israel" paraphrase.

He built an AI-queryable database of Charlie's own video, then used it. His ballistics deep-dive is the version of the rifle argument most people have actually seen, and his paved-crime-scene episode is among the most-watched pieces on the case.

He asks the question the forensic lanes do not: not how, but what Kirk represented and what removing him was meant to accomplish. Reaches Black and religious conservative audiences no other program on this list touches.

A left-populist host arriving at the same questions as the right-wing ones, which is why this FBI critique is hard to wave away as partisan. He interviewed Joe Kent about being told to stop, and hosted the crossover episode.

Eleven to fourteen million listeners an episode, and the case has barely touched the feed. Investigators treat him as the largest unused amplifier rather than a source — and this page is the watch-list for the episode that would change that.

An attorney who read the full confession texts on air and convened trial lawyers to argue the forensics. She was also on stage with Charlie six days before he died, and later said she and Tucker Carlson were "under serious threat."
A business operator's framework applied to a political killing: panels that put people who disagree in one room and let them argue it out. Useful when the evidence is contested rather than missing.
Frame-by-frame video work that TPUSA and Erika Kirk's legal team reportedly answered with a cease-and-desist. One of the very few independent programs to draw direct legal pressure over this case.

A former Navy SEAL and CIA contractor took the security-detail interview nobody else got. When the question is what a protective detail should have done that afternoon, this is the credentialed answer.
Multiple shows a day, an insider's map of who decides what in Washington, and no interest in letting the case fade. Read for the institutional reading, not the forensics.

The maximalist end of the device and foreign-service theories, and by far the loudest. This site records the claims with their physics rebuttals attached, because the claims travel and the corrections do not.

He put a sitting counterterrorism director on camera to say the inquiry was stopped — arguably the single most consequential interview in the case. He is also one of three names discussed for Law 4 authority.

The evacuation clock most timelines on this site are built on, plus the Google Trends graphics and the Israel-motive thesis. Used more than almost any other single researcher here, and labelled as attributed claims throughout.

Hundreds of accounts, indexed one page each: ADS-B tracks, drone sightings, crack-thump acoustics, GRAMA threads. This is where the open-source work actually happened, with every claim attributed to whoever made it.

Texas corporate filings and county deed histories for the roommate's family, posted with a question about timing. The follow-up post — showing the sale was an intra-family trust transfer — is on the page too.

Waveform panels, a crack-bang gap of 0.08 to 0.14 seconds, and a conclusion that the source was 70 to 90 feet away at ground level. The method is real physics; whether those transients are crack and bang is disputed.

An independent journalist whose threads keep surfacing at the seams — the Hamptons donor meeting, the widow's shifting timeline, the custody-versus-Discord clock. Attributed claims, tracked wherever they touch the court record.
An attorney itemised what the State actually put on the record at the preliminary hearing. Both the prosecution-side and the skeptic-side pages on this site quote her, which is unusual and useful.

The 72-hour compilation most readers met first: donor-loss texts, an emergency Zoom, and the warning message. A viral template rather than authenticated documents, and the page is explicit about which is which.
A same-day frame reading with two claims that need separating: something moving past a split second before impact, which anyone can check, and a ricochet mechanism, which video cannot establish.
An aggregation account whose screenshots became evidence — the alleged $150 million offer, the leaked texts about Ben Shapiro. Archived because they circulated widely, not because they were verified.
The reply-chain questioner who keeps asking why two separate video systems that should have recorded the surrender reportedly produced nothing at all.

The counterweight. He argues the camera set and the cumulative evidence are overwhelming, and he goes after the largest independent investigators by name. Kept here because a record with only one side is not a record.

The account behind the PETN-in-the-mic-wire video, plus the SUV glass, the Valhalla thread and the autopsy framing. Every claim on the page carries its counterargument, because the claims outrun the corrections.

The physics skeptic the device theory has to get past: a 32-gram clipped mic rockets away rather than driving a stable jet, and a PETN-class event should leave flash, smoke and torn fabric. The strongest version of the other side.

The director of the National Counterterrorism Center says the FBI shut his inquiry down before he could run his leads out. He stepped down in order to say it on the record — which is what separates this from an anonymous thread.

An arm-to-arm search found nothing. A K-9 pass found nothing. Then federal agents arrived, sent local officers back over the same ground, and a towel-wrapped rifle appeared — the reported sequence skeptics keep returning to.

A records request returned roughly fifty documents: two men warning campus police the night before, an email trying to reach Charlie, and an alert failure — with every name blacked out. The university reportedly holds more and has declined to release them.
Roughly 600,000 files went to the defense; the DNA-mixture data, ballistics scans and chain-of-custody logs reportedly did not. Critics call it volume used as concealment rather than disclosure.

The FBI director reportedly called the stairwell images "enhanced." They went out on the evening the suspect was already in custody — and critics say the morning and afternoon figures do not look like the same man.
The released rooftop clip reportedly starts at 12:23:34, with the runner already moving. The whole argument is about the seconds before that — the ones nobody has published.

Locks, shadowbans and limited-visibility warnings for engaging the wrong posts, alongside a witness reportedly told to delete his own footage. Suppression does not prove a cover-up, but it does decide what survives online.

The majority citizen finding is that the fatal event was an explosive device, and this is where that argument lives — hardware, procurement, four-channel audio, and the fragments reportedly found in the SUV.

Photographs reportedly released by Candace Owens show the inside of the vehicle that carried Charlie to hospital. Analysts point at the glass on the seat and ask what tempered glass was doing anywhere near a rifle wound.
A .30-06 round carries roughly 3,950 joules. Commentators argue the wound described publicly does not match that energy — the arithmetic that makes the government's rifle account hard to accept.

Every weapon and ballistics thread in one memo: the Mauser narrative, the ATF's "could not be identified or excluded" language, the energy mismatch, and the alternative calibers. Read it before quoting any single ballistics claim.

A US Army-contracted HADES jet reportedly flew low and slow within two miles of campus, about twenty minutes after the shot and three hours before it. If it was tasked, someone holds airborne sensor records of that afternoon.

Candace Owens called it the yellow plane. An Egyptian-registered Falcon 7X reportedly sat near Provo from September 4 and left the country in the hours around the killing, leading a cluster of foreign government jets trackers have followed for years.

The organization Charlie built, the donors who funded it, and the internal friction in the weeks before September 10. Read it alongside the motive threads; much of the reported pressure ran through here.

She called Charlie her best friend and brother, then ran the largest independent probe of his death. She also published the texts, the tipline and the SUV photographs the rest of the case now argues over.
A friend of Charlie's who put Joe Kent on camera to say the inquiry was stopped. He is also one of three names discussed for Law 4 investigator authority.
The man himself — what he built, what he changed his mind about in his final months, and who he told that he was afraid. Every other page on this site is downstream of this one.
Charged, not convicted. This is the record of what the State says it has and what independent researchers say does not fit — the DNA, the Discord messages, the Miranda clock and the photographs.

A dated timeline of Israel-related friction in Charlie's last months, with every entry labelled confirmed, evidenced, disputed or unverified. That labelling is the point; this is the thread most often argued without it.

Coverage settled on one story of how Charlie died within hours and has barely revisited it since. This section is the record of that settling — the wires, the live blogs, the panels, and what they stopped asking.

Four proposed federal laws that would force the 302s, the ballistics workup, the camera feeds, the 911 audio and the flight manifests into public view. Everything else on this site is an argument; this is the ask.
A week of sessions in Provo where the ATF ballistics, the rooftop, the autopsy and the phone evidence were finally tested under cross-examination. The day-by-day record of who said what on the stand.

The case that the charged man did not cause the death: ballistics that will not match, trajectory that will not work, timing that will not close. Presented as argument, with the counter-readings kept on the page.
Halted foreign inquiries, an ISR jet overhead, foreign phones, VIP flights and scene control. Indicators rather than proof — but they are the indicators an intelligence service leaves behind.

Search-trend claims that campus layouts, rooftops and named people were being looked up months before September 10, some reportedly from Israeli IP space. Trends data is noisy, and the page says so while laying the spikes out.

Rooftop, parking, CCTV, layout, Losee Center — the reported search strings read like a site survey, and they date to May through July 2025. The page carries the boring explanation too, because a large public campus generates traffic.

Midnight to midnight on Utah's clock: the pre-dawn aircraft picture, the camera sightings from 8:07 AM, the 12:23:30 shot, the hospital run, and the evening flights. Every line labelled reported or claimed.
No counter-snipers, no Secret Service, six campus officers and a last-minute private detail. Rooftops overlooking the stage were reportedly nobody's responsibility that afternoon.

The plane very likely did not launch drones; it may have been a training plane, possibly there to waste investigators' time. If the people who planned for it to be there knew the crime would happen, that is a path to foreknowledge — not a claim, a question worth investigating.

Two federal postures at once — public statements that foreign intelligence was assisting, and an on-record claim that the counterterrorism inquiry into those same threads was shut down. Both sides are on the page.
Court restrictions, silenced witnesses and an agency that stopped speaking. The reason so much of this case is argued from screenshots is that the people who know are not permitted to talk.

A former special-operations figure says a senior CIA contact told him agency personnel were turned around at the airport by the FBI, and that the Oval Office was told and did nothing. His reported account, not a finding.
The claim is usually "no autopsy." The accurate version is harder to argue with: an autopsy appears to have happened, and the report is still not public.
Donor pressure, an Israel position that was visibly shifting, warnings he reportedly gave three people, and the geopolitics around them. Motive is where this case stops being forensic.

The most-discussed foreign service in the citizen threads, appearing across motive, phones at UVU, Egyptian jet logistics and access claims. Discussion, not a court finding — and the page is careful about the difference.

Fifty-eight days before he died, Charlie put a debate about Israel, Epstein and Mossad on his own main stage, then reportedly told Tucker Carlson to go max. The clearest dated turning point in the coalition fight.
Every person near this case, sorted by role rather than by theory — witnesses, officers, staff, family, and a dedicated cluster for the people who turned out to be distractions.
The part of this site that asks something of the reader: which bills to track, who to contact, and what to preserve. Reading is not the point; the records are.
A contractor says the courtyard pave-over was run by two men who work for the state of Utah, not by campus facilities. He did not name them publicly, and this page does not either.

Three people say Charlie told them, in his last twenty-four hours, that he thought he was about to be killed. No screenshot has been published, which is why it is the most consequential and least documented claim here.
Texts she published have Charlie writing that he was not sure he would live to see the end of this revolution. The day before he died he reportedly offered her the AmFest stage back.

An archive account whose specialty is the post that later disappears — a deleted security-firm statement, a deleted staffer post. Screenshots of deleted posts cannot be independently verified, which is exactly why someone had to keep them.

Two visual-comparison claims tying people near the case to Fort Huachuca — carpet, wall colour, a public promo photograph. Visual matches are the weakest evidence class this site tracks, and the page says so before it says anything else.
The motive checklist most readers meet as a single block: the donor break, the youth pipeline, the Gaza language. Reproduced plank by plank so each one can be checked rather than swallowed whole.

Flight-record research in the John Cullen tradition — why one aircraft waited thirty minutes at a gate, and what the Egyptian fleet transponders were doing. Ramp positions and work orders could answer these questions; argument cannot.

TPUSA's spokesman is the rare account here who is an organisational insider — source and subject at once. Text authenticity, the succession statement and the "Andrew" who reportedly received the September 9 message all run through him. No court has accused him of anything.
A citizen analyst who checks viral claims against arrival clocks, and who pushed back on the 9:24 AM contact story from inside the skeptic camp. That discipline is rarer here than the claims are.

A veteran voice who cuts across both camps: his ammunition commentary supports the exit-wound argument for a rifle, while his physics critique undercuts the exploding-mic theory. Useful precisely because he is not picking a side.
Jacket-fragment measurements argued to be too small for a .30-06 profile. It is the most falsifiable of the citizen ballistics claims — released lab documentation would settle it in an afternoon.

The donor-realignment reading of what TPUSA did after September 10, restated as attributed political interpretation rather than adopted. The page is blunt about the limit: policy reversal is not homicide.

An amplifier with insider framing — a bio reportedly listing prior TPUSA work, and the quote-tweet that carried the Joe Kent shutdown clip into the movement's own audience. Circulation, not documentation.

An automated answering account, recorded here as the fact-check layer rather than as adjudication. It is the site's clearest example of machine-generated rebuttal running in the same threads as the claim it answers.

One of the main carriers of Charlie's alleged final warnings — the compilation posts through which the kill-me quotes spread. A quote amplifier rather than a document source, and the page holds that distinction.

The raw claim inventory behind the Sam Parker profile: flight data, ballistics questions, the Israeli-IP search dates, the $150 million allegation. Every line is a post, attributed and dated, not a finding.

The section's clearest counter-example: colour-coded spreadsheets arguing most of the alleged tailing flights either never existed or happened on another continent. The site keeps it beside the claim it tries to falsify.

Six campus officers, no owned rooftops, and a hired firm that also did not control the high ground. This account's function is keeping rooftop jurisdiction framed as a police question rather than a private-security one.
A low-follower account whose single clip share moved a case debate — the Bates-stamped 6:25 PM Miranda transcript read aloud from a defense motion. The strength here is the document, not the poster.

Open questions about George Zinn's reported prior contact with the travelling group, kept specific instead of general. Zinn's obstruction admission is court record; whether anyone directed him is not.

One narrow, checkable claim: does high-frame-rate footage show fabric moving before the wound appears? That is answerable with original-resolution video and imaging expertise, which is why the site logs it despite the dispute.

Day-of frame reading from September 10 arguing the round struck a vest and ricocheted upward into the neck. The same account also alleged an on-air witness was planted — an unevidenced claim the site keeps as the point where the arc outran its proof.

Hearing-week summaries of what prosecutors actually put on the record: the agent testimony, the roommate text thread, the gray Challenger near the gun-recovery block. The closest thing to a public transcript, and firmly the state's framing.

The claim that the camera nearest the wound angle came down and its card came out within about five minutes of the shot, before the zone was secured. Narrow and testable: bystander video either shows it or it does not.

A same-day July 2025 tracker log putting Egyptian Falcon SU-BTT at a civil field in Omaha — not an Army base. It was posted before any Kirk narrative existed, which is why it is the check on every compilation written later.

March 31, 2026: a reported ballistics non-match filing and a sheriff's resignation landed the same day, and this account made them one public question. Both items are documentary; the line drawn between them is commentary.

A conduit for insider-styled tips — black debris from inside the shirt, a rifle recovery between six and seven PM, and local officers who say they offered rooftop coverage and were told the detail was covered. Consequential if true, unverifiable as posted.

One narrow forensic question pulled from hearing coverage: the roommate reportedly described the message from Tyler as automated. If delivery metadata bears that out, the impulsive-confession framing loses its spine.

A skeptic who aims at both camps: weeks after the foreign-nexus statements there was still no evidence package, and still nobody can name one clinician who treated Charlie Kirk. A blocked inquiry is a lead, not a substitute for disclosure.

The official account of the surrender, preserved inside a thread that otherwise runs on suspicion — full credit to a retired colleague the family trusted. Small account, structural role: it defines the version that records would confirm or contradict.

Not an observer. The man who ran the private detail and rode in the SUV, whose own statements supply the pre-event text about student-accessible roofs, the reply that they were covered, and the two distinct sounds. Status: Alive; no court has found wrongdoing.

An alibi video only settles location if the location can be established. Other accounts say the carpet, trim and yellow wall match Fort Huachuca interiors; no metadata accompanies the claim, and this site asserts no identification.

The records lane: requests, denials, appeals. Its GRAMA production surfaced the paving texts dated the day after the killing while the scene was still locked, and its request for campus camera footage came back denied and under appeal.

The March 2026 seal fight reached the public largely through this account — a defense motion to seal the ATF report, ballistics described as inconclusive against the Mauser, and a press coalition opposing the seal.

One clip from the first hour: a well-sourced commentator on live television saying Charlie Kirk had a pulse, minutes before the death was announced. It cuts both ways — early uniformity may be broadcast chaos rather than choreography.

The account behind the state-actors clip and the line that our government stopped Joe Kent from investigating foreign involvement. It also carries the unverified counts: a second bullet at the scene, five unknown DNA profiles on the rifle.

Watch a claim mutate. The phone count at UVU drifts between eleven, twelve and sixteen depending on who is retelling it, and this account stacks it against a separate security-contact allegation — rhetoric the site records rather than adopts.

An amplification node rather than a source: the foreign-phones allegation passing through and picking up drift on the way. Useful for watching how a number changes hands, not for establishing what the number is.

The clearest surviving example of the shot-in-the-heart framing arriving by live television rather than by social-media retelling. It is the primary artifact that the official neck account has to be measured against.

Charlie Kirk's own X account, silent since September 10, 2025. His final week is evidence in itself — including the September 3 post amplifying Epstein survivors who said they would compile their own list of abusers.

One witness, two stations, about an hour apart: a chest account and then a neck account. This is the compilation that made the first-hour wound discrepancy impossible to wave away, with the witnesses treated as witnesses rather than suspects.

An account that refuses to sit on one side — pushing the State's surveillance package while stress-testing the provenance of the Israel-pressure retellings. Both roles run against the colloquy in which a prosecutor reportedly confirmed there is no footage of the shot itself.

A self-described former breacher's thread placing a shaped charge in a crucifix pendant rather than the microphone. Its author doubles as a rebuttal source against the mic version — proponents put the alleged device in three different places, and that is the weakness.

The strongest publicly posted benign reading of the Egyptian airframe timeline, kept because a flight thread carrying only the suspicious half is not a record. Weigh it against SU-BTT sitting at Provo through the event window.

Court reporting from Provo focused on what the public was not allowed to see. Its running record of non-broadcast rulings and sealed filings is the raw material for the argument that secrecy outlived the gag order's actual text.

The rebuttal half of the case's most contested procedural question: hearing summaries arguing custody did not begin before the Discord messages were typed. Observer notes, not transcripts — and the reason the site does not call that timeline settled.

Two small documentation threads that turn out to matter: a question about a changed booth position at the venue, and a chronology of the press briefings during the window when the suspect-in-custody alerts reversed.

Mainstream coverage is where most readers meet the ballistics doubt, and where inconclusive quietly became non-match. The distance between those two words is the whole argument, which is why the headline itself is logged here.

In an authentication fight, who put the screenshots into circulation matters as much as what they show. This account sits in the provenance lane of the alleged confession images, and its attribution claim has to survive primary records.

A timestamped claim of a second moving figure in the roof footage at the second of the shot, taken from a public court stream. It either survives frame-level analysis of the original or it does not — which is exactly the point.

The annotated SUV seating diagram behind the vehicle-occupant threads, carried here without its original caption. That caption is the site's standing example of material that fails the publication bar: serious, unverified accusations against named living people.

An amplifier for the strongest procedural argument in the case — that the accused was already in custody when the confession messages went out. Miranda paperwork, server metadata and hold-room video would close it in a day.

The entry-angle argument in its most cited form: the geometry of a rooftop shot set against the reported wound location. It cannot be closed either way while the autopsy report stays sealed, which is why it keeps circulating.

The viral breakdown of the 112-page GRAMA release — institutional failures logged at UVU the night before the shooting, with document numbers attached. The same account ran live hearing broadcasts, including counsel saying the family had not seen the video evidence.

The strongest documented voice on the other side: a data researcher defending the charged narrative and condemning attacks on Erika Kirk. The site keeps it because a lane with only one side in it proves nothing.

March 31, 2026 seen from the temporal-clustering school — a resignation and a reported inability to match the fragment to the rifle landing in public awareness on the same day. The site records the correlation and declines the causation.

The single documented amplifier of the witness-intimidation allegation — a UVU student who says a "free trauma counseling" session ran two hours behind a door locked from the outside. No therapist, agency or police report has ever been named, which is exactly what would move it from story to record.

A named proponent in the most contested OSINT lane on the site: pre-event Google Trends activity on the hospital, the surgeon and the rifle-drop locations. Skeptics answer that Trends is sampled noise at single-digit volumes, and the page keeps both readings.

The transparency-win side of the 2026 court fight — a judge refusing to seal records and letting cameras in. The page sets those wins beside what stayed sealed: the autopsy, the full ballistics appendices, the unredacted warrants.

Flight-tracker screenshots that put the "blue plane" SU-BND powered up on the Provo tarmac about twenty-one minutes before the shot and dark an hour after, without departing. Presence is not involvement — but transponder windows are checkable, and argument is not.

One of the densest claim compilations on the site: dispatch audio, the man who reportedly removed SD cards from cameras facing Charlie, a Mauser described but a Remington pictured. Every line is an attributed claim with its source post, several with the site's own corrections attached.

The overflow file for the same account — the casing engravings, the dispatcher who says no autopsy was done, the four separate changes of clothing the official story requires. Read the primary page first; this one carries the exhibits that did not fit.

He was on stage feet away, and his phone footage became a primary artifact for other people's analyses — including the claim that an infrared reflection traces back to a grey van behind the stage. He reportedly warned there were too many buildings for the venue.

Both edges of fast aggregation in one feed: a man named and pictured as the shooter within minutes who was released without charge, and, months later, some of the most-used courtroom reporting of the hearing days. A case study in what speed costs.

The March 31, 2026 pairing that went everywhere — a sheriff resigning after thirty years and the ATF reportedly unable to conclusively match the bullet, posted as "surely a coincidence." Temporal clustering is not causation, and the page says so out loud.

A transmission node for the alleged Charlie Kirk Israel quotes — the remarks about leaving the pro-Israel cause that reached most readers through a handful of X compilations. If authentic they reshape motive analysis; the primary materials have never surfaced.

A viral clip asks which Turning Point staffer was reportedly talking with the accused on the quad hours before the shooting — and cites a 9:24 AM arrival that conflicts with the 8:29 AM one in law-enforcement references. Quad camera footage from that window would settle it.

The reported recipient of a TPUSA cease-and-desist letter that, per Candace Owens' account, conceded the point at issue: a media production drone flew before the event while security's counter-drone request was denied. The letter itself has never been published.

A press account in the room documenting the court's "effective immediately" order to stop broadcasting exhibits after a leak. Whether that is ordinary courtroom order or information lockdown is the argument; that the order happened is not.

One pointed observation in the autopsy-transparency lane: the medical examiner who became the public face of the wound explanation was a Texas official who reportedly did not perform the autopsy. He is accused of nothing — the question is why the examiner of record stayed out of view.

A 270,000-follower AI-tutorials account that periodically routes assassination commentary into a tech audience — the rejected-offer claim, the Valhalla remark, the bomb-dog allegation. A case study in cross-audience amplification, where every underlying claim belongs to someone else.

The distinction this account pressed in real time is the whole identification dispute: hearing video reportedly shows positioning and flight, not a trigger pull. If no frame shows the shot being fired, the rooftop figure is linked to it by inference.

Story compression in action — nuanced reporting squeezed into one-sentence posts that reached tens of thousands in a day, including a government jet reportedly pulled from public tracking and the halted foreign-ties inquiry.

The public-access side of the 2026 secrecy fight: a judge denying a bid to close the preliminary hearing and block cameras. The site tracks those camera wins beside the digital forensics, medical files and warrants that stayed locked.

The argument skeptics of the device theory still have to answer: why crews allegedly dug ten inches of dirt out of the courtyard and repaved it in under seventy-two hours. Rapid repair can be crisis logistics — but the scene is gone either way.

July 2026 summaries of the leaked texts — including the claim that a rifle was left at a drop point and could not be retrieved because vehicles were still lingering. Screenshot dumps are chain-of-custody problems until a court authenticates them.

A small, datable node in the succession-skepticism discourse — circulating the argument that the eulogy read more like a fundraising appeal than a tribute. Recorded explicitly as opinion about tone, not a claim about anyone's conduct.

Two preserved screenshots that both belong to the scene-integrity question: a before-and-after comparison of the media layout at the site, and a four-panel study of the "pellet gun man" arrested in Provo the same period. He was never charged in the assassination.

Inside the device camp, an argument about which device: the lapel microphone rather than the pendant, and the claim that September 10 was the only time Charlie wore two of them. Adds the AES plant explosion weeks later as timing, not causation.

Narrative-pressure commentary rather than evidence — who stayed quiet about the AES explosion, and how a confession story might be rebuilt under trial stress. The site records the circulating language and rates it exactly that low.

The Utah governor's official account, which appears here twice over: as the source of state-side statements on the record, and as the handle citizen investigators tag when they want a testimony answered. Nothing here alleges wrongdoing by him.

A reproducible challenge rather than a theory: timestamped stills mapping the Losee Center egress at about twenty-five seconds, and the arithmetic question of whether the manhunt was thirty hours or thirty-three. Republish the stills and it either holds or it does not.

Threads that work as an index of what is still unresolved — the halted foreign-entanglements inquiry, the paved courtyard, the energy doubts, the chain-of-custody fights — while explicitly leaving guilt to a jury. Its media-handling allegation needs a named agent and a date.

Not an investigator: an AI assistant whose automated replies became the default statement of the official-narrative-adjacent counterargument in citizen threads. Useful as a record of which claims circulate and how the mainstream framing answers them — never as primary evidence.

A barometer for what the mainstream-right media cycle believed and when — the Discord logs sold as a confession two hours before turn-in, then the courtroom-access wins. Researchers use the feed to date when a narrative entered circulation, then check the docket.

Keeps the sharpest version of the fragment question alive: a courtroom bullet finding can confirm a projectile without proving a rifle match. Its medical-examiner search material is the weakest tier of claim on the page, and the page says so.

A post that cannot be a retrofitted narrative because it is timestamped four weeks before the shooting: someone close to Charlie reportedly said he believed Israel would kill him if he turned. On the day itself, asked to confirm, the account replied with one word.

The reporting that named which private firm is said to have been guarding Charlie that day — and a rival founder's account of being "stabbed in the back" over how the detail changed hands. Firm identity anchors every downstream question about the rooftop.

A high-volume claim stream built on one observation repeated many ways: no exit wound and no blood on the banner behind him. From there it argues a planted rifle, a low-velocity projectile and a patsy — attributed claims, each with its source post.

An amplifier node for the "Kirk was turning on Israel" clip corpus — the segments used to argue a late break with donors and policy. Excerpts travel faster than context, so the page sends readers to the originals.

This site's own author, held to the same standard as everyone else here: the .30-06 energy comparison, the Utah autopsy-release law that arrived months before September 10, and the documented throttling of the account that published them.

The distribution layer for the two claims most central to the not-the-assassin argument — fragments that reportedly cannot be conclusively matched, and the lead investigator testifying he learned about the paving of the scene from the news.

The flight-tracking account behind several Planes pages: an Air Force jet reportedly going dark near Fort Huachuca, and N1098L descending to 300 feet to loop Orem on the morning itself. Sensitive flights lawfully fly dark — the timing is still checkable.

The account that carried the Israel and donor-pressure threads to the largest audience — the object on the roof that disappeared, the missing autopsy, and the argument that the man charged is a patsy. Claims with sources attached, not findings.

The account that preserved and circulated the only public interior imagery of the SUV that carried Charlie from campus — staining, a pale fragment, debris some read as tempered glass. Authentication and lab testing are the open items nobody has closed.

Brady discipline, post by post: raw DNA data files the defense says exist but were never produced, and the thirty-four seconds the official story leaves for changing clothes, disassembling a rifle and leaving the roof. Specific enough to be answered.

The October 2025 post that started the remote-deletion thread — witness footage allegedly vanishing from phones nobody touched, carried to 270,000 views. Reach is not confirmation, and the site says so: forensics on one such phone would settle it either way.

A Fox News host carried the security contractor's own words — "We were told it would be handled" — to a national audience. That is what makes rooftop responsibility a mainstream dispute rather than a fringe one.

Two witness accounts could not both be true — heart and neck — so this account proposed body armor and a fragmenting round to reconcile them. Another investigator later reported Kirk wore no armor at all.

Relay and correction work: a tip about a speeding RAV4 whose driver reportedly flashed an FBI badge, and a one-day date fix that moves Kirk's reported break with the pro-Israel cause to within a day of the shooting.

Frame-level scrutiny of the final seconds — who glanced at whom on the security detail moments before the shot. The account poses these as oddities rather than proof, and the site keeps them that way.

The prosecution-leaning end of the citizen debate: leaked Discord logs, an unsealed warrant reporting prints at the roof jump site, and scouting-loop testimony. Useful precisely because it argues the other side of the pages around it.

Did a foreign outlet confirm the death before the earliest realistic pronouncement window had even closed? No outlet has published a first-publication timestamp ledger, which is exactly why the question is still open.

The post that put the bin Laden shooter on the record: "I've never seen a shirt move like that". Two decorated veterans said it looked like an explosion, and framed it as opinion demanding transparency, not forensics.

One node in the screenshot ecosystem behind the reported donor texts — the paraphrase about leaving the pro-Israel cause. No underlying message log has been authenticated publicly, which is the whole problem with the quote set.

Pairs personnel departures with missing recordings: a sheriff resigns, a campus officer resigns, and the roof body-cam footage is gone. The account asks who, if anyone, contracted the "shoot me" distraction.

The widest claim set on the site from a single account — a low-velocity projectile from behind, drones over the courtyard, and an ISR aircraft loitering nearby. Read it as a catalogue of testable hypotheses, most still untested.

Utah state experts reportedly cannot confirm the bullet found in Charlie came from the Mauser recovered in the woods. The counterpoint travels with the claim on this site: inconclusive is not exoneration.

The highest-volume amplifier in the scene-alteration record — the paver emergency interview clips, the ten-months-later revisit footage, and the transport SUV's fate. Questions asked at scale, and recorded here as questions.

Not a commentator — a participant. The former counterterrorism-center director says his own foreign-ties review was stopped before he could run down every lead. On-record statements, which the FBI has not endorsed.

Photographs of a rifle wrapped in a towel inside a cardboard box in the woods, and a timeline tension beside them: a camping trip discussed for months against a UVU event announced roughly fourteen days out. See Weapon and Rifle.

Amplifies the claim that searches for the hospital, its surgeon and the medical examiner spiked from Israeli and Washington IP ranges before September 10. Unverified search data — and the most-argued unverified data on the site.

The drone-denial claim: Kirk's detail reportedly asked for aerial surveillance and campus police declined. Six UVU officers, a private detail of about twelve, rooftops unsecured — that is the staffing picture the claim sits inside.

Courtroom narration that became the source clip for the body-cam gap: twenty-seven minutes of footage ending on the roof, reportedly because a battery died at that moment. Recorded as an open question, not an accusation.
Hosted the repost claiming Candace Owens and Tucker Carlson were warned on September 10 that they were on a target list. Unverified, and logged here only as a claim that circulated that day.

Two of his own posts, timestamped the day before and the day of, became discussion objects online. The site records the juxtaposition of timestamps and nothing more — no foreknowledge is alleged, and the quoted 2013 post concerned an unrelated subject.

Transponder analysis of an Army ISR jet making low passes near Orem before and after the shot. The open question is whether that week's ISR activity was routine training or something a subpoena should reach.

A broadcaster's own chyron is the evidence here — a split-screen frame presenting Skyler Baird to a national audience as an eyewitness. Everything commentators built on those interviews afterwards is a question posed by posters, not a finding.

Court-watch notes from the hearing where the autopsy entered evidence — gunshot wound to the neck, homicide, fragments recovered — while the judge kept the full report from the public. The narrative exists; the document does not.

The podcast that put Joe Kent's first-person account into mass circulation: his center reviews assassinations in parallel with the FBI for foreign ties, and his review ended early. The fullest version of a halt previously described only secondhand.

An anomaly list that keeps getting reshared — weekend excavation and paving, no bomb dogs, no roof protection, K9 non-alerts during the gun search. Attributed allegations, gathered in one place; see FBI Investigation.

Frames the reported August 2025 Hamptons gathering as an intervention, and the invitation that followed as a last warning. That framing belongs to the poster; no court has found any attendee threatened anyone.

Enters the record sideways — through screenshots of its own threads, filed in the photo clusters beside Candace Owens material. A reminder that on X the surviving archive is often a picture of a post rather than the post.

Published what it described as unsealed search-warrant texts between the accused and his partner, including an intent to surrender on his own terms. Powerful prosecution material if authentic — an authentication fight if not.

The intelligence scope fight in a handful of posts: a review of possible foreign assistance, and the claim it was shut down from above. Attributed political claims — with an on-record anchor in Kent's own account.

Asks what the charred-fragment photographs are supposed to be: why is there burned material inside the SUV? The fragment was never independently identified or tested, and lighting artifacts cannot be ruled out.

Video analysis of the seconds after the shot, focused on a phone reportedly raised to an ear before aid appeared. The poster frames it as a question about who was called — explicitly not as proof of anything.
Keeps one claim in circulation: the recovered fragment reportedly could not be matched to the alleged weapon. The site carries the standard counterpoint beside it — see the sealed ATF report.
